topic.title: Latent Dynamical Systems and Continuous-Time Prediction
topic.area: Continuous Models and Scientific Machine Learning
topic.overview: This topic learns hidden states and transition rules from sequences of observations. It includes stochastic state-space models, neural differential equations, irregularly sampled time series, and theoretical prediction guarantees. A representative probabilistic model learns dynamically relevant latent states without a parameterized reconstruction decoder, aiming to separate controllable structure from distracting visual detail.
topic.whyItMatters: Useful dynamics models must represent what changes predictably, not just compress individual observations. Handling noise, irregular timing, and environmental variation is central to reliable forecasting and to models that can support intervention or control.
topic.evolution: Early representatives learn qualitative or example-based descriptions of dynamics. Later work develops interpretable continuous-time models and neural controlled differential equations. Recent studies investigate decoder-free latent identification and spectral approaches with guarantees for specified classes of nonlinear systems, linking flexible modeling to explicit learnability conditions.
openQuestions: When are learned latent states identifiable and useful for control?
How can long-horizon errors be bounded when observation noise and environmental dynamics both change?
